sam_sales: Quick sync — BlueHarbor asked if we can run a short POC with a customer-supplied model (they call it minerva-xl-14b-v1). They want low-latency chat + retrieval augmentation. Can SE/infra confirm compatibility and any blockers?
priya_se: Do we have the model artifact format? HF tar / safetensors / ggml? Also what's the context length they need?
sam_sales: They've attached HF safetensors, tokenizer files, config.json. Target ctx = 32k tokens.
priya_se: 32k is big — runtime can support it but depends on KV cache layout and memory. Two initial checks: tokenizer compatibility (sentencepiece vs bpe) and whether model uses rotary vs ALiBi. If tokenizer mismatches we need a tokenizer adapter.
kevin_infra: Memory math: minerva-xl-14b @ 4-bit quant + 32k KV means per-request KV can be ~2–3GB depending on kv format. For sustained concurrency >6 we should target Dedicated with A100s (or A40s with sharding). We can also shard the KV across pods but that adds latency.
priya_se: Also need to know if they require exact-fp logits (no quant) — customer said quality-sensitive but willing to try 4-bit. We'll run a quality delta eval on their eval set. SE tasks: variant build (4-bit/8-bit/raw), tokenizer validation, and a quick perf sweep. ETA ~3 business days if artifacts are clean.
maya_security: Security checklist: since it's customer-supplied model, we need an SCA & license review, plus sign-off on model provenance. For Private deployments we can keep artifacts in their VPC. For Hosted, we need to ensure the model binary never lands on multi-tenant hosts and enable KMS-backed envelope encryption. Also prepping the security questionnaire — I'll ping legal for IP/license Qs.
sam_sales: Any special infra or infra-onboarding steps we should tell the customer? They're trying to decide between Hosted trial vs Dedicated POC.
kevin_infra: For Hosted trial: we can run a single-node Hosted sandbox but we must pin it to an isolated runtime and use cached KV to avoid noisy neighbors — this increases cost. For Dedicated POC: reserved node group + autoscale off for determinism. If they want 32k native ctx, recommend 2x A100-80GB or 4x A40 with sharding.
sam_sales: Pricing question: what's the rough uplift for an isolated Hosted sandbox and the Dedicated min-cost for a week POC?
priya_se: Ballpark: isolated Hosted sandbox (1 node, pinned) ~= $4k/day (includes DSP+ops), Dedicated minimal footprint (2x A100 reserved for a week) ~= $18k–22k for the week depending on network/egress and KMS add-ons. Variant validation fee (one-time) = $1,500 (includes perf sweep + quality regression check). Note: exact quote from finance required.
maya_security: Also flag: legal will require a data handling addendum if they feed any PII. If they want Private we can avoid that but requires network setup lead time (~5 business days).
priya_se: Ops runbook snippets we will include in POC packet. Example upload command for their artifacts:```
# customer uploads model to secure staging
rw model upload --name minerva-xl-14b-v1 --format hf --files model.safetensors tokenizer.json config.json --private --kms key-arn
```
sam_sales: Nice. Can you call out the high risk / blockers in one line so I can include in the sales email?
priya_se: High risk: 1) tokenizer mismatch requiring adapter (adds ~1 day), 2) 32k KV memory overhead impacting latency at concurrency >6 (may force Dedicated), 3) license/provenance issues from their artifact (blocks Hosted).
kevin_infra: Also note network egress for retrieval (if we call external vector DB) — could add latency and cost.
maya_security: I'll add security gating: SCA + license sign-off + DPA for PII. If they go Private much lower security friction.
sam_sales: Perfect. I'll send the email and ask them to provision a short eval set and give model artifact link. Priya — can you start the variant build once they upload?
priya_se: Yup — I'll watch the staging bucket and start the 4-bit variant build and QC once it's there.
deploy-bot: task created: SE-4571 "BlueHarbor minerva-xl variant build" assigned to priya_se, due 2024-08-07. :robot_face:
